Sam (AE): Quick sync — CustX wants a Private deployment POC. They asked for guidance on VPC peering vs PrivateLink, preserving client source IPs, firewall rules, and an estimated delta in monthly pricing vs Hosted. Can we sketch a handoff and callouts?

Priya (SE): I can draft the handoff. main questions: do they need inbound connections from our control plane? or just outbound to Redwood connectors?

Sam (AE): They want the control plane in our hosted control plane (API) talking to customer-managed data plane in their VPC. So outbound from their VPC to our connector endpoints. No inbound from internet.

Jordan (Network): OK — that means two practical patterns: 
1) VPC Peering + NAT egress from their side -> our public egress (simpler, but source IP rewritten)
2) Interface VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink) pointing at our connector -> preserves private path but we need to publish an interface endpoint service and they must accept endpoint.

Jordan (Network): NOTE: PrivateLink preserves source IP only if customer uses a proxy that forwards X-Forwarded-For; otherwise native TCP source IPs will be the ENI. We should call out source-IP-preservation constraints.

Maya (Security): Also check regulatory: they asked for SOC2 and KMS options. For Private deployments list: KMS/HSM integration available, audit log export, and option for customer-managed keys. Need to confirm if CustX requires key custody.

Priya (SE): For firewall rules — propose a minimal snippet customers can paste:

```
# Allow outbound to Redwood Private endpoint(s) IPs/hostnames
# TLS 443 outbound only
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d redwood-privatelink-us-east-1.example.net --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# Block other egress to public model endpoints if strict egress policy required
```

Priya (SE): Also include ports for health checks and metrics if they run sidecars. We can provide an allowlist of FQDNs and ASNs.

Sam (AE): Pricing question — what's the delta? quick bullets for customer: managed private control plane surcharge + per-hour dedicated connector footprint or monthly appliance license?

Priya (SE): For POC we recommend: 1 connector (t3-equivalent) + private endpoint provisioning. Pricing options: 
- Hosted API: pay per token (no infra charge)
- Private: one-time onboarding + monthly platform fee + infra usage (vCPU/GPU/GB) + optional SLA add-on

Priya (SE): I'll put estimated ranges in the handoff but flag this as "estimate — final depends on committed throughput."

Jordan (Network): Action items for NetOps handoff to customer:
- Confirm whether they will accept Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) OR prefer Transit/VPC Peering path.
- If PrivateLink: provide account-id + subnets for ENI + SG rules: allow inbound from redwood-private-service SG on 443.
- If Peering: provide VPC CIDR, route table to send to connector NAT, and whether they require source IP preservation; if yes, we'll discuss egress-proxy options.

Maya (Security): From security questionnaire POV, also ask: data residency (which region), retention window, expected retention type (logs/metrics/payloads), and whether they require monthly pen test attestation.

deploy-bot: deploy-plan-template.pdf uploaded to https://files.redwood.dev/handbook/poc-templates/deploy-plan-template.pdf :white_check_mark:

Sam (AE): Great. Priya — can you produce a one-page handoff doc with: architecture diagram (PrivateLink vs Peering), minimal SG/NACL snippet, required answers from CustX, and an estimated price range? Aim EOD tomorrow.

Priya (SE): Yep — will have draft by EOD tomorrow. I'll include a short table: pros/cons, cost levers (connector size, reserved vCPU commit), and common blockers.

Jordan (Network): I'll add a checklist for their NetOps: ASN, MGMT IP allowlist, test curl example. e.g.

```
# test TLS to PrivateLink FQDN (from inside their VPC)
curl -v https://redwood-privatelink-us-east-1.example.net/healthz --resolve "redwood-privatelink-us-east-1.example.net:443:10.10.1.12"
```

Maya (Security): I'll prepare the SOC2/KMS blurb for the doc and a short list of questionnaire items we can pre-fill.

Sam (AE): Thanks team. If CustX pushes for source IP preservation, call out the recommended pattern: customer-run egress proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For + keepalive to connector, or a transparent NAT solution in front with BYO EIP.

Priya (SE): Noted. I'll include both diagrams and one recommended config snippet for BYO EIP mapping.

Sam (AE): Perfect — I'll set up a 30m call with CustX for Thursday 16:00 PT after the draft is ready.

Priya (SE): Added to calendar, will ping when draft is up. :thumbsup:
